- User enjoys cooking and appreciates practical, simple recipes.
- Previous dinner-party plan:
  - Main: Lemon Garlic Chicken Breast with Roasted Vegetables.
  - Sides included a simple roasted vegetable medley, crispy roasted sweet potatoes, and cauliflower gnocchi.
  - Roasted vegetables: mixed vegetables with olive oil, salt, pepper, and optional herbs/garlic powder; roast at 425°F / 220°C for roughly 20–25 minutes.

- User bought a package of cauliflower gnocchi from Trader Joe’s and wants to try new recipes with it.
- Chosen cauliflower gnocchi recipe: brown butter sage sauce.
  - Suggested method: boil salted gnocchi and reserve pasta water; brown 4 tbsp unsalted butter until golden and nutty; crisp 2 tbsp fresh sage for 1–2 minutes; season, toss gnocchi in sauce, loosen with pasta water if needed, and optionally add Parmesan.
  - User thinks the brown butter sage sauce sounds amazing.
- User is making chicken fajitas for dinner tonight.
  - Basic recipe discussed: chicken strips marinated in lime juice, olive oil, garlic, oregano, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper for 30 minutes to 2 hours.
  - Cook sliced onion and bell peppers, then chicken until fully cooked; serve in warmed flour tortillas with optional avocado, sour cream, salsa, cheese, cilantro, and lime.
  - User plans to add onions, bell peppers, and fresh cilantro and parsley for the fajitas.
  - User is running low on olive oil and plans to buy more.
  - User feels set for dinner and has all needed shopping and cooking guidance.
- User asked how to keep cilantro and parsley fresh:
  - Refrigerate them rather than leaving them warm, dry, or in direct sunlight.
  - Best common method: trim stems and place herbs in a jar/glass of water, loosely covered, then refrigerate; change the water regularly.
  - For longer storage, chop and freeze in an airtight bag/container.
  - Herb keepers and specially designed refrigerator containers are also options.
